name: loihi_knn_query_latency
description: End-to-end latency of one approximate k-NN query over the 1M-pattern GIST-960 database on Pohoiki Springs (768 Loihi chips, unthrottled). The model is the pricer's own composition: t_cycle x latency_steps + the measured CPU wall the paper states is on the latency critical path (220us preprocessing + 300us tie-breaking postprocessing, Sec 5.4). SELF-CONSISTENCY, not independence: t_cycle's band comes from the SAME paper's Sec 5.1 sustained walls; what the case checks is that the sustained wall, the step count and the published query latency tell one coherent story through the real pricer. The flat wall under-charges the late-window slowdowns the paper attributes to x86 spike I/O (Fig 8 left rises to ~60us/step near the output window), so the prediction is expected to sit BELOW the measurement. Throughput is compared with a stated composition difference: the pricer inverts e2e (incl. the 520us CPU wall), while the paper's 366/s excludes pre/post (overlapped across queries) but includes the 230us reset off the latency path.

census_sources.timesteps: frady2020neuromorphic Sec 6.1: 'an integration window of 60 timesteps'; output spikes 'begin to arrive near timestep 80' (Sec 5.1) and the per-timestep trace of Fig 8 (left) runs through ~timestep 140, where the k=100 last outputs land -- the search occupies the full ~140-step span, not just the input window
census_sources.latency_steps: one query is one ~140-timestep search (input window + temporally-ordered output collection, Fig 8)
census_sources.sync_count: barrier sync is per timestep and already inside the sustained per-timestep wall t_cycle is built from
census_sources.host_macs: Eq. (3): the CPU preprocessing computes the ICA-transformed key (a 960 -> 500 projection, ~4.8e5 MACs); the WALL is measured (host_ops_s), so this census entry only states that host work exists
census_sources.host_ops_s: Sec 5.4: '220us of preprocessing on the CPU ... and 300us of CPU postprocessing ... contribute to the search latency' -- 520us on the latency critical path
